title: Why Is It So Hard to Cancel Amazon Prime?
description:
Amazon's own code name for the Prime cancel flow was 'Iliad', and the FTC case over it ended in a $2.5 billion settlement that is still paying refunds of up to $200.
#amazon #amazonprime #money #shorts

Sources: FTC press release (Sep 25, 2025); FTC complaint, FTC v. Amazon (Jun 2023) via Quartz and Yahoo/Business Insider; The Register (Jun 2023); Fortune (Sep 25, 2025); FTC Amazon refunds page and FTC press release (Sep 17, 2026); Amazon Q4 2025 results (Feb 2026); Marketplace Pulse
Photos: stockcatalog, shopblocks, Jorge Lascar, Blue MauMau, MDGovpics, Rob Ireton, Phillip Pessar (CC BY 2.0, Flickr)
first_comment: Be honest: do you still pay for Prime, or did you make it through the cancel maze? 📦

scenes.say: Amazon agreed to pay {$2.5 BILLION|two and a half billion dollars} over Prime's cancel maze.
scenes.source: FTC press release Sep 25 2025 ('FTC Secures Historic $2.5 Billion Settlement Against Amazon'); Fortune Sep 25 2025 ($2.5B: $1B penalty + $1.5B refunds)

scenes.say: Joining took one or two clicks.
scenes.source: FTC complaint Jun 2023 as reported by Quartz and The Register (enrollment 'in one or two clicks')

scenes.say: Canceling took four pages, six clicks and fifteen options.
scenes.source: FTC complaint via The Register Jun 21 2023 ('a four-page, six-click, fifteen-option cancellation process'); Quartz Jun 2023 (same wording)

scenes.say: Inside Amazon, its code name was Iliad.
scenes.source: Fortune Sep 2025 (FTC alleges Amazon internally called the process 'Iliad'); The Register Jun 2023 (internal code name)

scenes.say: The lawsuit says that's Homer's epic about the long, arduous Trojan War.

visual.quote: Fittingly, Amazon named that process 'Iliad,' which refers to Homer's epic about the long, arduous Trojan War.

scenes.source: FTC v. Amazon complaint (Jun 21 2023), verbatim as quoted by Quartz and by Yahoo/Business Insider

scenes.say: And the button to skip Prime said: No, I don't want free shipping.
scenes.source: FTC press release Sep 25 2025 ('Amazon can no longer have a button that says, "No, I don't want Free Shipping."'); Fortune Sep 2025

scenes.say: The government sued, and Amazon settled.
scenes.source: FTC sued Jun 2023, settled Sep 25 2025 (FTC press release; Fortune)

scenes.say: {$1 BILLION|one billion} in fines, and {$1.5 BILLION|one and a half billion} back to customers.
scenes.source: FTC press release Sep 25 2025 ($1 billion civil penalty; $1.5 billion consumer redress for ~35M consumers); Fortune Sep 2025

scenes.say: But here's the interesting part: Amazon's subscriptions made {$49.6 BILLION|forty nine point six billion} last year.
scenes.source: Amazon Q4 2025 results (Feb 2026): subscription services net sales Q1-Q4 2025 $11,715M + $12,208M + $12,574M + $13,122M = $49,619M; Marketplace Pulse ($49.62B in 2025, up 12%)

scenes.say: The whole settlement? About {18|eighteen} days of that.
If it caught you, refunds up to {$200|two hundred dollars} are still going out.
scenes.source: FTC press release Sep 17 2026 (per-consumer maximum raised from $51 to $200; automatic payments from Oct 1 2026); FTC Amazon refunds page (automatic refunds through April 2027, max $200)

scenes.say: Eighteen days. That's the real story behind the headline:
